title: More Monitoring, Less Pay: Active Ownership and Employee Compensation
eligible_reason: The paper's main analysis is a cross-sectional comparison of pay across ownership types within year-skill-occupation-region cells (absorb(industry firm_size yrsr)), not a DiD. The only DiD estimates (Table 5 private-equity buyouts, Table 6 column 1 hedge-fund ownership switches, Figures 4-5 event studies) are stacked difference-in-differences: the input files are stacked_analysis_data.dta with stack-specific unit FE (stack_frs) and stack-specific year FE (stack_year), treatment D = post x treated within each stack, clustered by stack_firm_id. Stacked designs are excluded by the protocol. Table 6 columns 2-3 are coarsened-exact-matching weighted cross-sectional comparisons. The shipped data are synthetic (10% random draws with noise added).
design_notes: Firm-year-skill-occupation-region pay cells from a compensation consulting firm (896 US firms, 20 million employee records). Main regressions: log_cwage_avg (also log_bwage_avg, stvp2base_avg, lti2base_avg) on ownership indicators ($owner_type) with aweight log_obs_count, absorb(industry firm_size yrsr), cluster firm_id. PE analysis: 9 buyouts (5 public-to-PE, 4 private-to-PE) matched on industry or industry and firm size, stacked; reghdfe log_cwage_avg i.D [aweight=log_obs_count], abs(stack_frs stack_year) vce(cl stack_firm_id). Hedge analysis: 10 switches from low to high hedge-fund ownership, same stacked specification. Event studies: ib2.rel2##i.treated on the stacked data (rel2 = years relative to treatment, t-1 omitted).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 9 PE buyouts and 10 hedge-fund switches at firm-specific years; the number of distinct years is not documented and the data are synthetic.
modern_estimator_note: Stacked DiD (Cengiz et al. 2019 / Baker et al. 2022 style) is used; no CSA/SA/BJS/dCDH.

specs.exclusion_reason: stacked DiD (stack-specific unit and year FE)
specs.treatment_var: i.D (D = post x treated within stack)
specs.treatment_definition: firm acquired by private equity in the stack's event year; controls are non-switchers matched on industry
specs.notes: Columns 2-3 (lines 41, 47) use industry-and-size matched and public-to-PE-only stacks.

specs.treatment_definition: public firm switching from low to high hedge-fund ownership (hhmed) in the stack's event year

specs.code_file: 7. replication/code/main pe - 2. run analysis.do (and main hedge - 2. run analysis.do line 91)
specs.treatment_definition: years relative to buyout/switch (t-3..t+2), t-1 omitted

data_files_note: README: real data are under a strict NDA with a compensation consulting firm; synthetic files are 10% random draws with noise added to pay variables and public-firm controls removed, so results do not reproduce the paper (Tables 2, 7, A9 cannot be run at all). Real-data code (code/) and synthetic-data code (code_synthetic/) are both shipped with logs.
software_notes: Stata 18 (reghdfe, estout, coefplot); Python notebook for Figures 1-2.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Even setting aside the stacked structure, the DiD analyses involve only 9-10 treated firms, so the leverage screen would likely fail.
